### `GET /cluster/qemu/cpu-flags`

```ts
proxmox.cluster.qemu["cpu-flags"].$get()
```

List of available CPU flags. Currently only implemented for x86_64, returns an empty list for aarch64.

Returns an array of `object`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accel` | `kvm` \| `tcg` |  | Acceleration type to check node compatibility for. — default `"kvm"` |
| `arch` | `x86_64` \| `aarch64` |  | Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture. |

### `GET /cluster/qemu/custom-cpu-models`

```ts
proxmox.cluster.qemu["custom-cpu-models"].$get()
```

List all custom CPU model definitions visible to the user.

Returns an array of `object`.

### `POST /cluster/qemu/custom-cpu-models`

```ts
proxmox.cluster.qemu["custom-cpu-models"].$post()
```

Add a custom CPU model definition.

Returns nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cputype` | string | yes | Name for the custom CPU model. The 'custom-' prefix is optional. — format `pve-configid`, ≤ 40 chars |
| `flags` | string |  | List of additional CPU flags separated by ';'. Use '+FLAG' to enable, '-FLAG' to disable a flag. There is a special 'nested-virt' shorthand which controls nested virtualization for the current CPU ('svm' for AMD and 'vmx' for Intel). Custom CPU models can specify any flag supported by QEMU/KVM, VM-specific flags must be from the following set for security reasons: aes, amd-no-ssb, amd-ssbd, hv-evmcs, hv-tlbflush, ibpb, md-clear, nested-virt, pcid, pdpe1gb, spec-ctrl, ssbd, virt-ssbd |
| `guest-phys-bits` | number |  | Number of physical address bits available to the guest. — min 32, max 64 |
| `hidden` | boolean |  | Do not identify as a KVM virtual machine. Only affects vCPUs with x86-64 architecture. — default `0` |
| `hv-vendor-id` | string |  | The Hyper-V vendor ID. Some drivers or programs inside Windows guests need a specific ID. |
| `level` | number |  | Maximum input value for the basic CPUID leaves the guest can query - that is the vendor (leaf 0), family/model/stepping and feature bits (leaf 1), cache and topology info (leaves 4 and B), and so on. Higher-numbered leaves are hidden. Setting '30' is a common workaround for Hyper-V boot failures on Windows guests running on recent Intel hosts. Only applies when the vCPU architecture is x86_64. — min 0, max 4294967295 |
| `phys-bits` | string |  | The physical memory address bits that are reported to the guest OS. Should be smaller or equal to the host's. Set to 'host' to use value from host CPU, but note that doing so will break live migration to CPUs with other values. — format `pve-phys-bits` |
| `reported-model` | `486` \| `a64fx` \| `athlon` \| `Broadwell` \| `Broadwell-IBRS` \| `Broadwell-noTSX` \| `Broadwell-noTSX-IBRS` \| `Cascadelake-Server` \| … (103 more) | yes | CPU model and vendor to report to the guest. Must be a QEMU/KVM supported model. Only valid for custom CPU model definitions, default models will always report themselves to the guest OS. — default `"kvm64"` |
